feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed for it. The evidence is iteration 1 (score 134.06, the best raced design), iteration 4 (score 122.26), and the iteration 0 baseline (score 49.8). Iteration 1 finished 1 of 20 oval trials at 1.65 s with base_speed 1.4, so 1.3 is a small cut that should still leave some time margin. Iteration 1 failed on the s-bend and slalom with 1.15 to 1.25 line-loss events per run and max_error at the 0.06 m limit, so line loss at the array edge is the main failure. The 16 mm, plus or minus 0.04 m array (0.02 m spacing) is supported by iteration 4, where the oval completion rate rose to 1 of 20 and max_error stayed near 0.063. Iteration 4 lost ground on the slalom with kp 3.7, so returning kp to 3.0 is a reasonable test, since iteration 1 was the best gain setting on the harder tracks. The kd rise from 0.5 to 0.8 is a larger change than the evidence alone demands. Oval steering_oscillation was 0.26 to 0.29 in iterations 1 and 4, so damping is justified, but the change is still large and combines with a speed cut and an array change. The candidate is valid and internally coherent, and it changes few enough fields that the race can be read against iteration 1 and iteration 4. Approve it, so the race gives telemetry that separates the damping and speed effects. After the race, read these in order. (a) If max_error still reaches 0.06 on the slalom with kd 0.8, turn-in lag is the limit, so move sensor y forward toward 0.05. (b) If progress stalls below 0.3 on the s-bend with no off-track exit, kd is too high, so drop it toward 0.6. (c) If steering_oscillation stays above 0.3 with line_loss_events still near 1 per run, the damping is not the fix, so keep kp at 3.0 and revisit the array edge geometry. Ignore line_loss_events as an array signal if they remain near 1 per run and the terminal event is the off-track exit.
requested_changes: If max_error reaches 0.06 m on the slalom while kd is 0.8, move sensor y from 0.03 toward 0.05 m, since iteration 1 and iteration 4 both show the off-track exit at bends, which points to turn-in lag.
If progress on the s-bend stalls below 0.3 with no off-track exit, lower kd from 0.8 toward 0.6, because iteration 4 showed kp and kd together can slow the robot without improving line keeping.
If the oval still completes but completion_time rises above about 1.9 s, return base_speed from 1.3 toward 1.4 with the same gains, since iteration 1 finished at 1.65 s at base 1.4.
